notes: The page starts with the continuation qui pour S variable about base change. Its opening text and smaller stability parenthesis are physically on scan101 but are absent from the assigned H page, which starts with (132). The main reader reports that H places the continuation at the end of its scan100 witness and has approved the corresponding placement row there. This report records that cross-page placement on the main reader’s observation; reader B did not inspect other page material. The page ends after pour les in the corollary; no completion, terminal point or material from another page is supplied.

The original and each native-resolution half were inspected once. Ten local crops were generated once from the original coordinates and all ten were actually viewed. Crops were enlarged by LANCZOS to 2800 pixels wide, except the foliation at 2400, then autocontrasted and mildly sharpened. Only nb-notation was rotated: minus 35 degrees, clockwise, with white expansion; its reported box remains [20, 1845, 700, 2345] in original coordinates.

Crop formula132, original box [300, 435, 1320, 565], was inspected even though it produces no substantive C/H correction. It establishes the full arrowhead, the prime on the target index, the number 132 and the final comma.

The text calls M_G a foncteur contravariant en G. Direct comparison of the actual ink shows that proposition a) writes G→G′, while (132) writes M_G→M_G′ and is then cited in that proposition. Under the usual meaning of contravariant, those matching orientations create an apparent local variance mismatch. Both written directions are preserved; no arrow or object has been reversed to repair the statement. This was an internal reading comparison, not a proof check of the proposition.

The author states in a) that a strict normalisation morphism induces an isomorphism of the modular multiplicities, and in b) that the map to the product for a sum of stable m.graphes is an isomorphism. These are the page’s assertions. No independent proof or verification of their hypotheses was performed.

The connector of (133) differs visually from the clear full arrow of (132): its only terminal decoration is a short downward stroke. A local down-harpoon/plain-shaft uncertainty is retained. The distinct comma after the product sign is also preserved, despite the cleaner formulas in both witnesses.

The diagonal NB has four baselines: On remplace la; notation Pi M_G par Pi-one M_G,; pour ne pas confondre Pi-one followed by the cancelled glyph; le signe du produit. Its live third Pi-one has an independent lowered 1. The unsupported avec in C and the unsupported final stop in C/H are removed. The resulting source syntax is retained without a repair.

The diagonal note overlaps the left side of (133) spatially but is not part of the horizontal formula. H’s alleged cancelled Pi-one-M_G/Pi-one group in (133) combines live note expressions and the separate struck note glyph. The note is transcribed as a margin item and its cancellation is recorded within that item.

For blind reading, the horizontal display and following sentence are grouped in B07, and the complete overlapping diagonal note is grouped independently in B08. B08 contains all note formulas, both written Pi-one indices and the cancellation. The corollary Pi-one is included in B09. The actual displayed numbers 132 and 133 and the prose reference 132 are all included; no other display number is introduced.

The long underline after Ainsi stops at en, before the separate G. Proposition, strict, iso., NB and Cor have the underlines recorded in the TeX. The dots absent after Proposition and Cor are not supplied from H.

The body words morphismes de normalisation remain live. De m.graphes stables is a separate interlinear addition attached before the following point. In b), the raised m.graphes stables replaces the struck phrase, while the small struck de before G is a separate deletion; no live et or comma is supplied there.

The old phrase in b), the cancelled note glyph, the cancelled le and the small old f-like mark remain locally doubtful. In contrast, pour in the corollary remains live: the p is retraced, but there is no separate strike through the whole word. No extra deleted text is invented from the overtracing.
The pale 100 at the foot is separately inventoried as foliation and transcribed with margin. No dark authorial page number or date is visible; ms_page is empty.

The main reader independently viewed the original and all ten crops and agreed with M1146’s alternative, the product comma, the connector uncertainty, the literal NB wording, the other lexical and revision-state decisions, and the retained local doubts. No OCR, external research or TeX compilation was used.
